comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Re-measurement (2026-08-11) of LIMB 1 ONLY: the claim is a measurement artifact. Production CREATEs already carry `creation_channel="python"`.

Scope note up front: this addresses **limb 1** (`creation_channel` is still null). The fsck
per-env signed-rate limb, the `_seam` skip-logging limb, and their ACs are untouched by this and
remain valid, so **the ticket stays open**.

### Limb 1 cannot be true in code — there is no null-emitting path

The triage already flagged that `_lib_writes.py:91` defaults `_creation_channel` to `"python"`.
The real constraint is stronger and upstream of that default: `create_core`
(`_commands/composer.py:88`) declares

    creation_channel: str          # keyword-only, NO default

validated at composer.py:118 by `validate_creation_channel()` (which explicitly rejects
`"unknown"`) and stamped **unconditionally** into event data at composer.py:181. Every
CREATE-producing path must therefore declare a channel — omitting it is a `TypeError`, not a null.

All 13 construction sites, and none can emit null:

| site | value |
|---|---|
| `_commands/composer.py:88,118,181` (`create_core`, the single seam) | required kwarg, validated, stamped |
| `_commands/composer.py:305` (CLI `create`) | `"cli"` |
| `_lib_writes.py:91→125, 144→169, 191→215, 234→250, 545→569, 581→597` | `"python"` |
| `_mcp_writes.py:69, 91, 104, 172` | `"mcp"` |
| `_commands/idea.py:67` | `"cli"` |
| `_commands/session_log.py:135→149, 165→195, 250, 254` | `"python"` / `"cli"` |
| `_commands/identity.py:282→308, 340→391, 678` | `"python"` / `"cli"` |
| `_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:139, 221` | validated provider / `"jira"` |
| reducer `reducer/_processors.py:124` | `data.get("creation_channel", "unknown")` — **never None** |

The review-bot's own create sites — `review_bot/artifact_emit.py:102` and
`llm/code_review/finalize.py:62` — are plain `rebar.create_ticket(...)` with no
`_creation_channel`, so they take the `"python"` default. That matches the store exactly.

### The store contradicts the claim directly

Read-only extraction via `git archive origin/tickets` (tickets HEAD
`3618edf2263dd7f609cf9acf9808fa9d08b6f342`, 2026-08-11 18:26:18 -0700), 1981 CREATE files.
The `"python"` default landed in **`dfdac9d63a7107a76d4a3e78ce16fa18aa2e7b84`, 2026-07-17 00:49:14
-0700** ("creation-channel: record immutable genesis channel for CLI/MCP/Python").

* CREATEs **before** that commit: 533, of which null = **533** (100%).
* CREATEs **after**: 1448, of which null = **10** (0.69%).
* All 10 post-cutoff nulls fall in a single **4h21m window, 2026-07-17T00:59:31 → 05:20:30** —
  the lag before the deployed bot build picked up the merge. Three of them are reviews *of the
  creation-channel commits themselves*.
* **Zero null-channel CREATEs anywhere in the store after 2026-07-17T05:20:30Z** — ~25 days and
  1438 CREATEs.
* Restricted to the beb1 signing deploy (first signed CREATE 2026-08-09T13:39:17): **52 review-bot
  CREATEs at or after it, `Counter({'python': 52})`, null = 0.**

Env histogram for `code_review`: `python` = 1074, None = 166 (all pre-cutover).
Per-env: `b2b5c498` 157/157 null before → 1088 after with 10 null; `ade0f2ef` 354/354 → 333 with
**0**; `reconciler` 15/15 → 6 with 0.

Sampled review-bot CREATEs spanning the cutover:

| ticket id | CREATE timestamp | creation_channel | author | signed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| f05f-722b-6cdc-42a8 | 2026-07-17T05:20:30 | **None** (last ever) | Unknown | no |
| d3b2-3702-092f-4a62 | 2026-07-17T12:47:12 | `python` (first ever) | Unknown | no |
| 2b1f-3387-1330-441d | 2026-08-09T13:11:11 | `python` | Rebar Bot | no |
| 9232-64a9-a96b-4423 | 2026-08-09T13:39:17 | `python` | Rebar Bot | yes (first signed = beb1) |
| 671c-b741-664a-4b26 | 2026-08-11T11:37:53 | `python` | Rebar Bot | yes |
| 2051-f4d8-8d29-4f55 | 2026-08-11T18:21:54 | `python` | Rebar Bot | yes |

### The likely source of the false reading

`creation_channel` lives in `event["data"]`, **not** at the event top level. On a real recent event,
`event.get("creation_channel")` returns `None` while `event["data"]["creation_channel"]` returns
`"python"` — verified live on `2051-f4d8-8d29-4f55`. The audit that produced the beb1 tally also
read `author` / `author_id` / `author_sig`, which *are* top-level keys, and almost certainly read
`creation_channel` by the same top-level path — returning `None` for 100% of events regardless of
their actual channel.

That also explains the limb's own framing: "unchanged from the 8880 pre-fix events". A top-level
read is null for **every event ever written**, which is exactly the "unchanged" signature reported.
So the observation was real; the field path was wrong.

Cross-check that settles it: `rebar show f05f-722b-6cdc-42a8` (a genuinely channel-less legacy
CREATE) reports `creation_channel='unknown'`, **not** null — the reducer floor at
`reducer/_processors.py:124` means a null can never reach a reader even for legacy data.

### Verdict and recommendation

**Limb 1's AC — "Review-bot CREATEs carry a non-null `creation_channel`" — is already satisfied in
production** (52/52 post-deploy CREATEs = `"python"`, zero nulls store-wide for 25 days). It needs
no code change.

Not closing the ticket: three of its four ACs belong to the other limbs (fsck per-env 0%-signed
reporting, `_seam` logging when signing is SKIPPED rather than FAILED, held-out tests), and this
measurement says nothing about those. Suggested re-scope of limb 1: (i) fix the audit script's field
path to read `event["data"]["creation_channel"]`, and (ii) decide whether to backfill or annotate
the 166 pre-2026-07-17T05:20 review CREATEs that legitimately project as `"unknown"` — a historical
question, not a live defect.

All evidence gathered read-only; no repository or store state changed.

comments.body: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-12: AC2 standing per-env signed-rate fsck check APPROVED; 'loud' means logged/counted (require_authenticated stays advisory per ADR-0045). Limb 1 (null creation_channel) was disproven by measurement — see prior comment; scope the remaining work to AC2/AC3.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Scoped the description to the approved subset per the OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-12 comment: **AC2 (standing per-env signed-rate fsck check) and AC3 (_seam logs the signing-SKIPPED path) only**, plus held-out tests. Limb 1 (null creation_channel) is recorded as explicitly out of scope, not silently dropped — the prior re-measurement comment disproved it. require_authenticated stays advisory (ADR-0045); nothing in this ticket makes a write fail.

Premise re-validated against the code and the live store before claiming:
- AC3 confirmed at `_seam.py:327-359` — when `identity.signing_key` IS configured but `author_id` is falsy, control falls past the sign branch and, with require_authenticated off, returns with **no log line**. Only the signing-FAILURE path (line 341) logs today. That is exactly the beb1 silence.
- AC2 confirmed at `fsck.py:111-122, 259-264` — the authorship tally is store-wide and uncounted, so a single env at 0% signed hides behind another env's healthy volume.
- Read-only measurement over the live tracker (18 envs): four envs are 0%-signed, and all four are **dormant** (last event predates the store's first signed event). No env is both 0%-signed and active after signing adoption. So gating the new check on 'this env wrote at or after the store's first signed event' yields zero findings on today's store while still catching beb1's env b2b5c498 (0 signed / 8914 Unknown-authored, writing concurrently with the signing env ade0f2ef). That adoption gate is the false-positive guard and is pinned by its own held-out test.

File impact recorded. fsck.py is 779 LOC against the hard 800 cap, so the tally goes in a new leaf module fsck_authorship.py rather than growing fsck.py.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Implementation pushed for review: Gerrit change **1630** ('Make a silent unsigned writer loud'), commit 76da2bb7be on branch mynah-create-guard.

**AC3** — `_seam._apply_authorship` now emits a logger.warning on the cannot-sign path, naming the event uuid, the ticket, and which input was missing (no resolvable author_id vs no identity.signing_key). Signing stays best-effort; require_authenticated stays advisory (ADR-0045), so no write starts failing. The unconfigured fast path stays silent deliberately — warning on every write of an unsigned store would bury the signal — and that is pinned by its own test.

**AC2** — new leaf module `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_authorship.py` (EnvAuthorshipTally). fsck now emits `UNSIGNED_ENV:` as a COUNTED issue (in issue_count and in --output json issues[]) for any env_id that signs nothing, or authors everything Unknown, yet wrote at or after the store's earliest signed event. The tally is fed from the payloads Check 1 already parses, so it adds no filesystem pass. `unsigned_env` is deliberately NOT in _STRUCTURED_KINDS because that set parses the line head as a ticket_id and this head is an env_id — pinned by a test.

**RED verified before GREEN**: against unmodified sources the AC3 test fails on the exact assertion 'the signing-SKIPPED path must not be silent' and the AC2 tests fail on the missing module. 10 new tests, all passing; test_identity_3183_heldout and the 46 fsck/doctor/module-size tests still pass; make lint and make typecheck green; fsck.py is 795 LOC against the 800 cap.

**False-positive evidence on the live store**: ran the tally over all 24680 event files — **0 findings**, because all four 0%-signed envs are dormant. The check is quiet on real history and would still have caught beb1.

Note for the record: an attempted `git stash` in the code worktree (used to verify RED) failed and its `pop` pulled another worktree's WIP in with conflicts — the repo-global stash-stack hazard AGENTS.md warns about for the tracker applies to code worktrees too. Recovered with no loss (all 4 stash entries intact, conflicted files restored from HEAD) and the RED check was redone with plain file copies instead.

compiled_state.description:
# Make a silent, identity-less writer LOUD (scoped to AC2 + AC3)

Split out of bug beb1. **Operator decision 2026-08-12: implement AC2 and AC3 ONLY.** The
original limb 1 ("review-bot CREATEs carry `creation_channel=null`") was **disproven by
measurement** and is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE — see the re-measurement comment: production
CREATEs carry `creation_channel="python"` (52/52 post-deploy, zero nulls store-wide for 25
days); the null reading came from reading a top-level key that lives in `event["data"]`.
"Loud" here means **logged and counted**; `identity.require_authenticated` stays advisory
per ADR-0045 — this ticket does NOT make any write fail.

## Why this matters

beb1 (a review bot writing ~8900 unsigned, `Unknown`-authored events) ran for a MONTH
undetected because the failure was silent at two layers that this ticket closes:
`_apply_authorship` returns with no log at all when no identity resolves, and `fsck`'s
authorship line is a single store-wide tally, so one env writing 0% signed is invisible
behind another env's healthy volume.

## Confirmed mechanism (read from the code, 2026-08-11)

- `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:327-359` — `_apply_authorship` signs only when
  `author_id AND signing_key`. When `signing_key` IS configured but `author_id` is falsy,
  control falls to the cannot-sign branch; with `require_authenticated` off (the default)
  it **returns silently**. Only the signing FAILURE path (line 341) logs.
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:111-122, 259-264` — the authorship tally is summed
  store-wide into one advisory, uncounted text line. There is no per-`env_id` breakdown,
  so the per-env signed-rate analysis that eventually found beb1 remains a one-off script.

## Measured baseline (live store, read-only, 2026-08-11)

18 envs. Four are 0%-signed (`a7f6c5e0` 6 events, `37a1e8e8` 5, `00000000-…` 4,
`58e9f32e` 2) and **all four are dormant** — their last event predates the store's first
signed event. No env is both 0%-signed and active after signing was adopted. So the
adoption-gated rule below reports **zero** issues on today's store (no legacy noise), while
beb1's env `b2b5c498` (0 signed, 8914 `Unknown`-authored, writing concurrently with the
signing env `ade0f2ef`) WOULD have been reported.

## Acceptance Criteria

The approved subset only — AC1 (creation_channel) is out of scope, see below.

- [ ] **AC2** — `fsck` reports, as a **counted** issue (`UNSIGNED_ENV:` line, `issue_count`
      and `--output json` `issues[]`), any `env_id` that has at least one event and either
      **0 signed events** or **every event authored `Unknown`/absent**, gated so it fires
      only when the store has adopted signing AND that env wrote at or after the store's
      earliest signed event. Dormant pre-signing envs are NOT reported.
- [ ] **AC3** — `_apply_authorship` emits a `logger.warning` when signing is **SKIPPED**
      for lack of a resolvable identity (or a missing signing key under the gate), naming
      the event uuid, the ticket, and which of the two inputs was missing. It must remain
      best-effort: no write may start failing because of this ticket.
- [ ] Held-out tests for each: an fsck test asserting a 0%-signed active env is counted AND
      that a dormant pre-signing env is not (the false-positive guard), and a `_seam` test
      asserting the skip path logs at WARNING with the reason and still writes the event.

## Implementation notes

`fsck.py` is 779 LOC against the hard 800 cap, so the tally lands in a new leaf module
`src/rebar/_commands/fsck_authorship.py` (an `EnvAuthorshipTally` that `_scan` feeds from
the JSON it ALREADY parses in Check 1 — no extra I/O pass) and `fsck.py` gains only the
wiring. The new `unsigned_env` kind is deliberately NOT added to `_STRUCTURED_KINDS`: that
set makes the transform parse the line head as a `ticket_id`, and this head is an `env_id`.

## Out of scope

creation_channel (disproven), backfilling the 166 legacy `unknown`-channel review CREATEs,
and any change to `identity.require_authenticated` enforcement.

Wire the tally into _scan Check 1 and append counted findings (AC2)
